properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 26 at 9:31PM CDT until October 27 at 3:00PM CDT by NWS Midland/Odessa TX
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Midland/Odessa has issued a Flood
Warning for the following rivers in Texas...

Rio Grande at Rio Grande at Presidio Vehicle Bridge affecting
Presidio County.

For the Rio Grande...including Rio Grande above Rio Conchos near
Presidio,  Texas, Test Forecast Point A, Rio Grande at Presidio
Vehicle Bridge, Rio Grande below Rio Conchos near Presidio,  Texas,
Rio Grande near Castolon,  Texas, Rio Grande at Johnson Ranch near
Castolon,  Texas, Rio Grande at Rio Grande Village,  BBNP,  Texas,
Rio Grande near Dryden,  Texas, Terlingua Creek near Terlingua,
Texas...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.
This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...Rio Grande at Rio Grande at Presidio Vehicle Bridge.

* WHEN...From this evening to Tuesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 12.0 feet, the river reaches bankfull, after which the
flood plain between the levees begins to flood.  No damage is
expected. At 15.5 feet, the river reaches minor flood stage, and
flooding between the levees occurs.  No damage to structures is
expected. At 20.0 feet, the river reaches moderate flood stage,
inundating the plain between the levees.  Erosion of the levees is
likely.  Water may seep through the levees, flooding adjacent
farmland. At 22.9 feet, the river reaches major flood stage.  While
water remains between the levees at Presidio, areas downstream may
experience significant flooding.  FM 170 downstream of Presidio
will flood in low spots.  Farmland along the river will be
inundated. At 25.0 feet, the river remains between the levees at
Presidio, although continued flows at this level could cause damage
to the levees.  FM 170 downstream will likely be flooded and
impassable in spots.  Farmland around the river will continue to
inundate. At 25.8 feet, the river reaches record stage for the
period of record (1978).  A higher stage was reached in 1932, but
the exact stage is unknown.  FM 170 will be flooded downstream of
Presidio.  Farmland around the river will remain inundated. At 28.2
feet, the river reaches record stage for the period of record
(1978).  A higher stage was reached in 1932, but the exact stage is
unknown.  FM 170 remains flooded downstream of Presidio.  Farmland
adjacent to the river remains inundated. At 30.0 feet, The top of
the levee is reached, and water will begin to overtop the levees.
Major flooding of Presidio and surrounding farmland is likely.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 3:30 PM CDT Monday the stage was 42.1 feet (12.8 meters).
- Bankfull stage is 12.0 feet (3.7 meters).
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 3:30 PM CDT Monday was 42.1 feet (12.8 meters).
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage just
after midnight tonight and continue falling to 4.1 feet (1.2
meters) Saturday evening.
- Flood stage is 15.5 feet (4.7 meters).
- Flood History...No available flood history.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

through flooded areas.

The next statement will be issued Tuesday morning at 945 AM CDT.

properties.areaDesc: Culebra
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 26 at 9:38PM AST until October 28 at 6:00AM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...High Rip Current Risk, life-threatening rip currents.

* WHERE...North-facing beaches of Culebra.

* WHEN...Through late Tuesday night.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
properties.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

NWSheadline: HIGH RIP CURRENT RISK REMAINS IN EFFECT THROUGH LATE TUESDAY NIGHT

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 26 at 3:30PM HST until October 29 at 5:00AM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
properties.description:
A trough moving over the state from the southwest will bring
abundant tropical moisture late Tuesday through at least Wednesday
night. Heavy rain and isolated thunderstorms are expected to produce
flash flooding, and while the greatest flood threat will be focused
over Oahu and Maui County, all islands are at risk.

* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...All main Hawaiian Islands.

* WHEN...From Tuesday morning through late Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...Significant flooding may occur due to the overflow of
streams and drainages. Roads in several areas may be closed, along
with property damage in urban or low lying spots due to runoff.
Landslides may also occur in areas with steep terrain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Heavy showers and isolated thunderstorms with intense rain rates
are expected to develop on Tuesday and continue through Wednesday
night as a trough moves over the state. While the greatest flood
threat will be focused over Oahu and Maui County, all islands are
at risk.
properties.instruction:

should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to one half foot of
inundation above ground level expected along shorelines and
tidal waterways (9.6 to 9.8 feet Mean Lower Low Water at Fort
Pulaski).

* WHERE...In Georgia, Coastal Bryan, Coastal Chatham, Coastal
Liberty and Coastal McIntosh Counties. In South Carolina,
Beaufort and Coastal Jasper Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through Tuesday evening.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 7 AM to noon EDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Saltwater inundation will impact some roads. Rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tide will occur around 9:15 AM Tuesday at
Fort Pulaski. Saltwater inundation will be possible 1 to 2
hours before and after high tide.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Visit water.weather.gov for additional water level and flood
impact information.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Lake, FL; Volusia, FL
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 26 at 9:20PM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.Persistent gusty northeast winds are causing river levels to rise on
the St Johns at Astor, currently in Moderate Flood Stage. The river
is forecast to remain in Moderate Flood Stage, perhaps beginning a
slow decline late week into the weekend.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Major flooding occurs with water entering
many structures on canals and along the river. Long duration
flooding will occur, with levels taking weeks to months to return
below flood stage. Water rescues will be necessary. River Road
becomes inaccessible, with 1 to 2 feet water depth in numerous
homes on Wildhog, Possum, Bonnet and Snail roads. Roads along Blue
Creek are inaccessible with major flooding of homes on Otter,
Branch and Chestnut roads. Camp South Moon Road and Juno Trail are
inaccessible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 PM EDT Monday the stage was 3.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 PM EDT Monday was 3.8 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 3.8 feet
just after midnight tonight.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Tuesday afternoon at noon EDT.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE

properties.areaDesc: Socorro, NM
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 26 at 7:14PM MDT until October 30 at 12:00AM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in New
Mexico...

Rio Puerco Near Bernardo affecting Socorro County.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Puerco near Bernardo.

* WHEN...Until late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...At 24.0 feet, old Highway 60 bridge is overtopped. At
23.0 feet, streets in the village of San Francisco between
interstate 25 and the Rio Grande just south of Bernardo are being
flooded. Water levels in the Lower Rio Puerco have not been this
high since July of 1944. The nearby railroad bridge may also be
flooded. Further rises will impact Interstate 25 traffic.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 6:00 PM MDT Monday the stage was 24.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 18.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 6:00 PM MDT Monday was 24.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to gradually fall into minor
flood stage early Tuesday morning, then rise again to 21.8 feet
Wednesday morning before falling below flood stage Thursday.
- Flood stage is 19.5 feet.
- Flood History...No available flood history.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

The next statement will be issued Tuesday afternoon at noon MDT.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 26 at 7:03PM MDT until October 29 at 4:00AM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Pueblo has issued a Flood Warning
for the following rivers in Colorado...

Purgatoire River Near Las Animas affecting Bent County.

For the Purgatoire River...including Las Animas...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...High flow is traveling down the Upper Purgatoire from recent
rains, and may lead to flooding near Las Animas.

* WHERE...Purgatoire River near Las Animas.

* WHEN...From late tonight to late Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...At 9.0 feet, Minor Flood. Minor agricultural flooding
occurs into low lying areas along the river.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 6:15 PM MDT Monday the stage was 6.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 7.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage just
after midnight tonight to a crest of 10.5 feet tomorrow evening.
It will then fall below flood stage Wednesday afternoon.

- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 10.5
feet on 08/19/2004.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Tuesday morning at 715 AM MDT.

properties.areaDesc: Jeff Davis, TX; Pecos, TX; Reeves, TX
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 26 at 7:51PM CDT until October 26 at 11:45PM CDT by NWS Midland/Odessa TX
properties.description:
FFWMAF

The National Weather Service in Midland/Odessa has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
East Central Jeff Davis County in southwestern Texas...
West Central Pecos County in southwestern Texas...
South Central Reeves County in southwestern Texas...

* Until 1145 PM CDT.

* At 751 PM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 2 and 5 inches of rain
have fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Balmorhea Lake and Saragosa.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.
